newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end flat, blue chips help turnover.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end flat, blue chips help turnover.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed flat as investors remained sidelined ahead of next month's local polls, but selected foreign buying supported turnover, brokers said.

The all share index closed 0.30 points up at 618.40. Price gains outnumbered losses by 20 to 14. Central Finance rose two rupees to 240, Hayleys 2.75 to 195, Lanka Orix Leasing two rupees to 152, Ceylon Tobacco 75 cents to 32.75.
"As expected, results coming out look good and under normal conditions the index should rise," said Shafi Waheed, a trader at CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch.
"However, many investors are staying out to see if there will be violence ahead of next month's election," he said.
Meanwhile, results for the 1996 financial year ended December 31, 1996 and the nine months in the financial year to March 31, 1997, look encouraging, brokers said.
"Most of the results which have come out so far have augured well for 1997," said one.
Turnover was 25.4 million rupees on 1.3 million shares. Foreign buying was 12.09 million and selling was 7.3 million.
The main trades were 525,000 Asian Hotels and 21,700 Hayleys. --Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
